text:
Anita: kicked off a per-channel scaling + layer-skip sweep for AWQ on redwood-alpha-65B this morning. baseline: fp16. quick summary below, details in threads.
Mike: nice. what's the motivating signal? large negative MSE on layer 28 during int8/GPTQ runs?
Anita: exactly. we see a handful of layers (24-30 range) with huge outlier channels that drive LM loss regression after quant. skipping layer or applying per-channel scale reduces drop.
Jon: can you paste the scan output?
Anita: posted the scan snippet: 
```
> layer_scan --model redwood-alpha-65B --quant awq --mode per-channel-scan --out /tmp/scan.json
layer 24: max_channel_outlier=12.3, median=0.02, mse=0.18
layer 25: max_channel_outlier=15.9, median=0.01, mse=0.32  <-- bad
layer 26: max_channel_outlier=1.2, mse=0.01
layer 27: max_channel_outlier=9.1, mse=0.09
```
Sarah: wow layer 25 is the culprit. did you try skip-layer quant (force fp16 for that layer)?
Anita: yes. two strategies tested: (A) skip layers [24,25] (keep fp16) + AWQ elsewhere, (B) per-channel scaling (compute per-outlier-channel gain, clamp) + AWQ globally.
Mike: metrics? latency and quality tradeoffs?
Anita: short numbers from eval harness (head 10k prompts, MRR & exact-match proxies):
- fp16 baseline: MRR=0.712, EM=0.423, tail latency p95=210ms
- AWQ all-layers: MRR=0.694 (-0.018), EM=0.405 (-0.018), p95=160ms
- AWQ + skip [25]: MRR=0.708 (-0.004), EM=0.419 (-0.004), p95=162ms (+2ms)
- AWQ + per-channel scaling (k=3 clamp): MRR=0.709 (-0.003), EM=0.420 (-0.003), p95=164ms
- GPTQ int8 whole-model: MRR=0.695 (-0.017), EM=0.402 (-0.021), p95=150ms
Jon: so skipping layer 25 recover most of the accuracy with tiny latency hit. great. how many params switched to fp16 if we skip that one layer?
Anita: only ~0.6% extra memory, because it's mostly FFN weights in that layer. cost delta negligible for dedicated nodes.
Sarah: what's the ops impact on batching? does skip break kernel fusion?
Anita: small. the runtime creates a fallback kernel for that layer; we lose a micro-batch fusion at that layer boundary but end-to-end throughput is within 3% of AWQ-only.
Mike: any risk of regressions on other eval sets? can we run the safety/qa eval suite?
Anita: queued parallel runs on eval-bot, also running longer context tests (2k tokens). initial signals look consistent but want full sweep (overnight).
eval-bot: queued job 4829: per-channel-sweep x 4 configs (awq, awq+skip, awq+pcscale, gptq-int8). ETA ~10h
Jon: one more thought — try hybrid: per-channel scaling for top-2 outlier channels + skip layer for remainder. might get parity with fp16 and lower mem.
Anita: good idea. I'll add hybrid config to the sweep. also logging the per-channel gains; we may be able to bake these into compile-time quant params.
Mike: when you have the full run, can you post the small table for deploy-runbook? we'd want guidance: "skip if max_channel_outlier > X AND mse > Y" or auto-fallback rule.
Anita: will do. tentative rule: if max_channel_outlier > 10 and mse > 0.15 => skip layer. otherwise enable per-channel scaling with clamp k=3. I'll validate thresholds after full eval. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sarah: thanks — also add a smoke test for A/B rollout. canary to 1% traffic and compare token-level KL vs baseline.
Anita: noted. adding rollout recipe to the PR. short-term deploy profile: AWQ default, skip layers [25] for model family redwood-alpha-65B-v1, fallback to fp16 if >0.5% tokens differ on canary.
Mike: perfect. ping when results land. :thumbsup:
